p: A cluster of restaurants serving jokbal, a dish of marinated and boiled pig's feet. Various preparations, including cold sliced versions, are available.

A local eatery that serves milmyeon (wheat noodles), a food item associated with Busan. The restaurant offers both the chilled broth version (mul milmyeon) and the spicy mixed version (bibim milmyeon).
The main item served here is budae jjigae (army stew), a dish cooked at the table in a large pot. Ingredients typically include ham, sausage, baked beans, kimchi, and ramen noodles in a spicy broth.

This alley features multiple eateries specializing in dakbal (spicy chicken feet), a popular local late-night dish. Visitors can choose between boneless or bone-in versions, usually accompanied by alcoholic beverages.
Offers several varieties of traditional Korean stews (jjigae) served in individual earthenware pots (ttukbaegi). Options usually include kimchi jjigae, doenjang jjigae, and sundubu jjigae.

An area containing several small, traditional pubs (jumoek) specializing in makgeolli (Korean rice wine). Various regional makgeolli types and accompanying traditional side dishes (anju) are served. This spot is popular among locals for…
A cluster of hoega (Korean-style beer bars) that specialize in draft beer and fried chicken (chimaek). This area provides a lively, high-energy environment typical of Korean urban nightlife.

A series of large, multi-room karaoke complexes (noraebang) that require the purchase of alcohol and food along with the room rental fee. This venue type is intended for group entertainment and late-night socializing.
